evals.prompt: Design a public endpoint that creates exports and may take minutes to complete.
evals.expected_output: The contract covers long-running operation semantics, identifiers, status, errors, and idempotency.

evals.prompt: Define an order-created event consumed by several teams with at-least-once delivery.

evals.prompt: Add a field and enum value to an API used by old mobile clients that will remain deployed.
evals.expected_output: The skill evaluates consumer compatibility rather than assuming additive syntax is automatically safe.

evals.prompt: Design a payment-intent mutation where clients may timeout after the server commits.
evals.expected_output: The contract defines idempotency/preconditions and safe behavior for unknown outcomes.

evals.prompt: Use api-design to review a selected greenfield HTTP/JSON lookup contract. The human intentionally chose HTTP 200 for a valid USER_NOT_FOUND business result. A proposed body is {"success":false,"status_code":404,"code":"USER_NOT_FOUND","data":null}. Correct that contract and compare a normal HTTP 404 design without changing the selected business policy. Show the actual HTTP status and body for each.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the intentionally selected business absence as HTTP 200 with body status_code 200 (if included), success false and stable USER_NOT_FOUND code. Shows normal HTTP 404 as another valid/default design with transport-consistent body status. Does not emit HTTP 200/body404, insist all not-found must use HTTP200, or erase application outcome into transport status. Optional/null semantics remain explicit.

evals.prompt: Use api-design for an authorized client that receives two HTTP 404 failures. RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND means the selected row was deleted and should be refreshed; MAKE_DO_DEFINITION_NOT_FOUND means an activity prerequisite needs repair while the draft stays. A teammate proposes using message.includes("definition") because both have status 404. Messages will be localized. Show the minimal server/client contract and classification; do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Requires distinct stable machine-readable codes/types and exposes them through the client classification boundary to the feature. Shows classification by identity, never parsing localized messages or status alone. Preserves different recovery: refresh deleted row versus repair prerequisite and preserve draft. Treats identity as consumer contract while respecting resource-hiding/auth policy rather than revealing forbidden state.

evals.prompt: Use api-design to settle this mutation contract. Operation op-17 may have committed but its response was lost. A retry with the same idempotency key gets HTTP 404 MAKE_DO_DEFINITION_NOT_FOUND after a definition was removed. A teammate wants to mark op-17 NOT_APPLIED and enable a new-key resubmission. No authoritative receipt/status has been retrieved yet. What can the API/client conclude and what resolves it? Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Keeps original op-17 outcome unknown/unresolved; the later 404 describes that attempt, not proof the original was unapplied. Preserves original operation key and pending recovery state, seeks authoritative operation receipt/status/reconciliation, and avoids new-key blind retry/duplicate submission. Distinguishes success, definitive rejection, and unknown outcome separately from retryability. Must not state NOT_APPLIED/rollback or definitive rejection from the later failure alone.
